name: Oxytocin
route_note: IV infusion for induction or augmentation of labour; IM or IV injection after delivery
originator: Vincent du Vigneaud (synthesis); Parke-Davis and Sandoz (pharmaceutical products)

discovery.by: Vincent du Vigneaud and colleagues, Cornell Medical College
discovery.note: Determined the nine-amino-acid sequence of oxytocin and synthesised it, the first polypeptide hormone made in the laboratory.

tagline: First synthesised peptide hormone; induces labour and prevents postpartum haemorrhage
summary: Oxytocin is a nine-amino-acid peptide hormone released from the posterior pituitary that stimulates uterine contractions and milk ejection. Synthetic oxytocin is used to induce and augment labour and is the WHO-recommended first-line drug for preventing and treating postpartum haemorrhage.
mechanism: Oxytocin binds Gq-coupled oxytocin receptors on myometrial cells, activating phospholipase C and raising intracellular calcium, which increases the frequency and force of uterine contractions. Receptor density rises sharply in late pregnancy, so the uterus becomes much more sensitive at term.

After delivery, sustained contraction of the uterus compresses spiral arteries at the placental site, reducing bleeding. Oxytocin also contracts myoepithelial cells in the breast and has weak antidiuretic activity due to similarity with vasopressin.
uses: Prevention and treatment of postpartum haemorrhage
Adjunct management of incomplete or inevitable miscarriage

history.title: Uterotonic extract
history.detail: Henry Dale shows that posterior pituitary extracts contract the pregnant uterus.

history.title: Separation
history.detail: Oliver Kamm and colleagues at Parke-Davis separate the oxytocic and pressor principles of pituitary extract.

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Vincent du Vigneaud sequences and synthesises oxytocin.

history.title: Nobel Prize
history.detail: Du Vigneaud receives the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the first synthesis of a polypeptide hormone.

history.title: WHO guidance
history.detail: WHO recommends oxytocin as the uterotonic of choice for preventing postpartum haemorrhage.

history.title: CHAMPION trial
history.detail: Heat-stable carbetocin is shown non-inferior to oxytocin, relevant where cold-chain storage is unreliable.

serious: water intoxication and hyponatraemia with prolonged high-dose infusion
safety.boxed_warning: Pitocin (US): not indicated for elective induction of labour (initiation of labour without medical indication).

facts: Oxytocin is on the ISMP list of high-alert medications because dosing errors can cause serious harm to mother and baby.
It loses potency at high temperatures, so it requires refrigeration in many supply chains.
